content: Pravastatin is a medication prescribed to help reduce levels of cholesterol and other fatty substances in the blood. It is used in conjunction with lifestyle changes such as a healthy diet, weight loss, and regular exercise. Pravastatin belongs to a class of drugs known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, or statins. It works by slowing down the production of cholesterol in the body. Excess cholesterol and fats can accumulate along the walls of blood vessels, a condition called atherosclerosis, which reduces blood flow and oxygen supply to vital organs like the heart and brain. Lowering cholesterol levels can decrease the risk of heart disease, chest pain (angina), strokes, and heart attacks. Pravastatin is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. It is important to take it at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication than prescribed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it, but not more frequently than once every four weeks. Continue taking pravastatin even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting pravastatin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to pravastatin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and non-prescription drugs, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as cimetidine, cyclosporine, ketoconazole, other cholesterol-lowering drugs (e.g., fenofibrate, gemfibrozil, niacin), and spironolactone, may interact with pravastatin. Your doctor may need to adjust your doses or monitor you for side effects. If you are taking cholestyramine or colestipol, take them four hours before or one hour after pravastatin. If you are using antacids, take them one hour before pravastatin. Inform your doctor if you have liver disease, as pravastatin is contraindicated in such cases. Let your doctor know if you consume large amounts of alcohol, have a history of liver or kidney disease, or are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking pravastatin, stop the medication immediately and contact your doctor, as it may harm the fetus. Do not breastfeed while taking pravastatin. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking pravastatin. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can increase the risk of serious side effects. To maximize the benefits of pravastatin, follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This includes foods like cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, soybean oils). Avoid high-fat foods such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (except cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of pravastatin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Pravastatin may cause side effects. Minor side effects include heartburn and headache. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; lack of energy; fever; yellowing of the skin or eyes; pain in the upper right abdomen; nausea; extreme tiredness; unusual bleeding or bruising; loss of appetite; flu-like symptoms; rash; hives; itching; difficulty breathing or swallowing; swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; and hoarseness. If you experience any unusual problems while taking pravastatin, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store pravastatin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests before and during treatment to monitor your response to pravastatin. Inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel that you are taking pravastatin before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
